notes.text: In the cloudy and dark day — In the time of general distress.
The fat — The powerful and rich. I will feed - I will judge and punish them.

glossa.text:
*A psalm in confession.* Confession is twofold; one is of praise, the other of sins. The confession of praise befits the perfect, the confession of sins those who are beginning *inicipientibus*; whence in this psalm the prophet admonishes to confession. ((CASS.)) This psalm teaches both to praise God unceasingly, and unceasingly to bewail our sins: because neither in evils is one to despair, nor in good things ought the mind to be lifted up. First he enjoins upon the perfect the chief kind of confession, that is, praise.

*Rejoice ye.* ((AUG.)) If the voice rejoices outwardly, etc., *as far as* and in what order and how wonderfully he made it. *All the earth.* Admonishing to praise. Not one corner of the earth does he exhort: but as he knows the blessing to have been sown everywhere, so from everywhere he requires jubilation. *Serve ye in gladness.* ((AUG.)) This servitude is not of bitterness, nor of indignation, but of happiness and of liberty. Let charity therefore make thee a servant, because truth has made thee free. Whence the Lord: *If you shall abide in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed: and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free ((Joan. VIII))*. 

*In gladness.* Because they are set free; not murmuring, as in the desert: whence he subjoins the reward.

*Enter ye into his sight.* It is a great thing to rejoice in the sight of so great a one. *Enter ye in.* ((CASS.)) Secondly, to those about to enter, the second kind of confession; nor let it be doubted, because mercy is with him.

notes.text: Since I heard of your faith and love — That is, of their perseverance and increase therein.
I cease not — In all my solemn addresses to God. To give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers - So he did of all the churches, Col. i, 9.

That the Father of that infinite glory which shines in the face of Christ, from whom also we receive the glorious inheritance, ver. 18, may give you the Spirit of wisdom and Revelation — The same who is the Spirit of promise is also, in the progress of the faithful, the Spirit of wisdom and Revelation; making them wise unto salvation, and revealing to them the deep things of God. He is here speaking of that wisdom and Revelation which are common to all real Christians.

The eyes of your understanding — It is with these alone that we discern the things of God. Being first opened, and then enlightened - By his Spirit. That ye may know what is the hope of his calling - That ye may experimentally and delightfully know what are the blessings which God has called you to hope for by his word and his Spirit. And what is the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints - What an immense treasure of blessedness he hath provided as an inheritance for holy souls.

And what the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe — Both in quickening our dead souls, and preserving them in spiritual life. According to the power which he exerted in Christ, raising him from the dead - By the very same almighty power whereby he raised Christ; for no less would suffice.

And he hath seated him at his own right hand — That is, he hath exalted him in his human nature, as a recompence for his sufferings, to a quiet, everlasting possession of all possible blessedness, majesty, and glory.

Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion — That is, God hath invested him with uncontrollable authority over all demons in hell, all angels in heaven, and all the princes and potentates on earth. And every name that is named - We know the king is above all, though we cannot name all the officers of his court. So we know that Christ is above all, though we are not able to name all his subjects. Not only in this world, but also in that which is to come - The world to come is so styled, not because it does not yet exist, but because it is not yet visible. Principalities and powers are named now; but those also who are not even named in this world, but shall be revealed in the world to come, are all subject to Christ.

And he hath given him to be head over all things to the church — An head both of guidance and government, and likewise of life and influence, to the whole and every member of it. All these stand in the nearest union with him, and have as continual and effectual a communication of activity, growth, and strength from him, as the natural body from its head.

The fulness of him that filleth all in all — It is hard to say in what sense this can be spoken of the church; but the sense is easy and natural, if we refer it to Christ, who is the fulness of the Father.

glossa.text: *Therefore.* The benefits conferred upon the human race, or upon the apostles, or upon the Ephesians having been enumerated, the Apostle subjoins what he thinks concerning their benefits, namely that he gives thanks, and asks that more be added, lest they be proud, but stretch beyond.
*That God,* etc. As if he should say: to obtain it I put forward not merits, but that he is God and the Father of Christ, etc.

*The eyes of the heart.* In his own image, therefore, know thou its author, who is not attained by bodily sense. Do not, therefore, think that God is attained by bodily sense, but with the eyes of the mind hear him. In the body, where the members are diverse, thou hearest in one place, thou seest in another. But in thy heart, where diverse members are not found, there thou hearest where thou seest. And to this end may he enlighten the eyes. *That you may know,* etc. This he says that they may be the more inclined: because when they shall fully know what the fruit of believers is, they will become the more inclined toward the cultivating of religion. Or thus: that hope be taken properly. And the sense is: That you may know what it is, namely his will *voluntas*; read *vocatio*, "calling", that is, how much the hope of eternal life avails, unto which he calls. And that you may know what the fulfilment of that hope is. Which he thus says: *And what are the riches.* Here he discloses what he understood by the name of hope: for he takes hope as the thing hoped for.

*What is the exceeding greatness.* The highest doctors shall have a certain increase of glory, beyond that which all shall have in common. For all shall have the same penny. *But star differeth from star in brightness ((I Cor. XV))*. *And there shall be diverse mansions in the house of the Father ((Joan. XIV))*.

*Raising him up,* etc. Now the example of the glory of the saints consists in the resurrection of the Saviour, that in it the faithful may know what has been promised to them. *At his right hand.* The right hand is the eternal beatitude which is given to the saints: the left is the misery which is given to the wicked. For by no form of body is God bounded and enclosed.

*Above every,* etc. This he says on account of the incarnation of the Son of God, that even having been made man he may be said to be above all the heavens, and above every creature, having his name by nature, not by adoption.

*Under his feet,* etc. By the feet full subjection is noted, and all things are deservedly subject to him, because they were made through him; or, the feet signify the humanity, because as the foot is the lower part of the body, so in Christ the lower nature is the humanity, which even the angels adore. *And him,* etc. After he has commemorated the dignity of Christ, he returns to us, showing that his dignity pertains to us; as if he should say: God so exalted Christ that this his exaltation pertains to us: because he himself is the head, and we the body, that we may partake of him. *The head.* According to the deity: because all were made by him, and also according to the humanity, by which the Church is joined to him, by nature and by grace. *For of his fullness we have all received ((Joan. X))*.

*His fullness.* Because he is filled up through them, yet being all things in all, here and in the time to come. Likewise. When those who have entered unto confession bend the knee to Christ, he is filled up, because those who withdraw seem to empty him. *All things in all.* Because the members confer nothing upon him, but he himself all things upon the members: because by his power they are what they are.

notes.text: Inherit the kingdom — Purchased by my blood, for all who have believed in me with the faith which wrought by love. Prepared for you - On purpose for you. May it not be probably inferred from hence, that man was not created merely to fill up the places of the fallen angels?

I was hungry, and ye gave me meat; I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink — All these works of outward mercy suppose faith and love, and must needs he accompanied with works of spiritual mercy. But works of this kind the Judge could not mention in the same manner. He could not say, I was in error, and ye recalled me to the truth; I was in sin, and ye brought me to repentance. In prison - Prisoners need to be visited above all others, as they are commonly solitary and forsaken by the rest of the world.

Then shall the righteous answer — It cannot be, that either the righteous or the wicked should answer in these very words. What we learn herefrom is, that neither of them have the same estimation of their own works as the Judge hath.
Inasmuch as ye did it to one of the least of these my brethren, ye did it to me — What encouragement is here to assist the household of faith? But let us likewise remember to do good to all men.
Depart into the everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels — Not originally for you: you are intruders into everlasting fire.
Then will they answer — So the endeavour to justify themselves, will remain with the wicked even to that day!

And these shall go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into life everlasting — Either therefore the punishment is strictly eternal, or the reward is not: the very same expression being applied to the former as to the latter. The Judge will speak first to the righteous, in the audience of the wicked. The wicked shall then go away into everlasting fire, in the view of the righteous. Thus the damned shall see nothing of the everlasting life; but the just will see the punishment of the ungodly. It is not only particularly observable here

1. That the punishment lasts as long as the reward; but,

2. That this punishment is so far from ceasing at the end of the world, that it does not begin till then.

glossa.text: *And when.* Being about to be delivered to the cross very soon, he set before them the glory of him who triumphs, that he might make up by this promise for the scandals that were to follow. After the parables about the end of the world, the Lord now sets forth the manner of the judgment to come.

*The sheep from,* etc. There shall be two orders in the judgment, namely of the elect and of the reprobate: but of the elect some shall judge, to whom it is said: *You also shall sit upon twelve seats, judging the tribes of Israel.* Others shall be judged, to whom it is said: *I was hungry and you gave me to eat.* Likewise of the reprobate, some who are outside the Church shall not be judged: others who shall be judged, to whom it is said: *I was hungry, and you gave me not to eat,* etc.
*The goats.* The he-goat is a butting and rank-smelling animal, which was offered for sins in the law, and it signifies sinners: nor does he say she-goats, which can have young.

*Blessed of the Father.* Advanced by the benefit of my Father to the obtaining of glory, in which you may reign without corruption, to which you have been predestined from the foundation of the world.

*Then shall they answer.* Not distrusting the words of the Lord, but either amazed at the greatness of the king's majesty; or because every good thing that they did seems little to them, whence it is said: *The sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come ((Rom. VIII))*, etc.
*Of these brethren.* My brethren and my mother are they who do the will of my Father.
*You gave me not,* etc. What does he deserve who has seized what belongs to another, if he is eternally damned who has not given anything of his own?

*Lord, when,* etc. They busy themselves to excuse themselves, as though they who were deceiving men could deceive God. But they have no excuse who would not be converted from evils and do alms; whence he adds: *As long as you did it not to one,* etc.

*Into everlasting punishment.* In vain therefore does Origen promise deliverance after many years to evil men and to the demons themselves. *Into everlasting punishment. ((AUG.))* In which matter Origen was assuredly the more merciful, who believed that the devil himself too and his angels, after punishments heavier according to their deserts and of longer duration, were to be rescued out of those torments and joined to the holy angels. But the Church has not undeservedly condemned him, both for this and for sundry other things, and chiefly for the blessednesses and miseries alternating without ceasing, and for the endless goings and returnings from those to these at fixed intervals of ages.

notes.text: In the cloudy and dark day — In the time of general distress.
The fat — The powerful and rich. I will feed - I will judge and punish them.
God's — Above all that are called God's angels, earthly potentates, and especially the false gods of the Heathen.
Hand — Under his government. Strength - The strongest or highest mountains.
Pasture — Whom he feeds and keeps in his own pasture, or in the land which he hath appropriated to himself. The sheep - Which are under his special care. Today - Forthwith or presently.

glossa.text: *Come, let us rejoice.* ((THEOD.)) King Josias was exceedingly pious, etc., *as far as* but the psalm is framed in the person of Josias, and of the priests of God. ((CASS.)) Concerning the time of grace, in which there is an entering into rest, the prophet, describing the praises of God, first invites the Jews, whom he foresaw to be able to resist Christ.

*His face,* etc. ((AUG., CASS.)) The sight of the judge to come, lest there be anything then in us to be sifted. *In confession.* ((AUG.)) Praising him, accusing ourselves, etc., *as far as* of which praise the psalm treats. *In psalms let us make a joyful noise.* *psalmi*; read *psalmis*, "in psalms" What we say in psalms, or do, let us feel in jubilation.
*Above all gods.* Or rather he calls men gods, over whom he is king, not over demons.
*For in his hand,* etc. ((CASS.)) After the greatness of the Lord foretold, he comes to his clemency.

*The sea.* ((AUG.)) The world, whose waves God confines within a bound, not suffering us to be tempted above that which we are able ((I Cor. X)); which waves also make increase for us, God working it, nor do the scandals hurt thee, which receive their measure from God.

*Come, let us adore.* ((CASS.)) First he called the untaught to exultation: now, the glory of God being shown, he calls to penance, which is the harder. *Let us weep.* ((AUG.)) If perchance you are solicitous concerning the sins which have made you far off, weep: a tear extinguishes the flame of sin which burns in the conscience. *Who made us.* Behold great confidence: for of thyself thou canst fail, thyself thou canst not remake, he remakes thee who made thee.

*And we are the people,* etc. ((AUG.)) Elegantly is the order of the words changed: He did not say the sheep of the pasture and the people of his hand, that thou mayest understand those very ones to be sheep who are the people, sheep of his hand, not those which from afar, because they are, and sheep which we did not make, but he himself by his own grace made us sheep.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Come, let us sing to the Lord, the great King above all gods.
We are his people, the sheep of his hand.
The Son of Man will come in glory and sit on his throne.
And he will know us by our mercy to the least.
God has seated Christ far above every rule and power.
He is head over all things for the church.
Come, let us worship Christ the King.
We bow before the Shepherd-King. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Lift your eyes to the throne at the end of all things, the Son of Man crowned in glory, the nations gathered before him like a shepherd dividing the flock.
Christ is King, and we are his.
Yet this King is the Shepherd who searches for the lost, binds up the broken, and carries the weak ones home.
Christ is King, and we are his.
He has been raised far above every ruler and power and given a name above every name, head over all things for us.
Christ is King, and we are his.
And he is known by this: a cup of water, a coat, a visit to the prison — as you did it to the least, you did it to the King.
Christ is King, and we are his.
So come, you sheep of his pasture, and bow before the Shepherd-King.
Christ is King, and we are his! Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Come, sing to the Lord, the great King above all.
Christ is King, and we are his.
The Son of Man comes in glory to the throne.
Christ is King, and we are his.
This King is the Shepherd who seeks the lost.
Christ is King, and we are his.
Come, let us worship Christ the King.
We bow before the Shepherd-King. Amen.
